newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DOWIE ENDS GOAL DROUGHT IN IRISH VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DOWIE ENDS GOAL DROUGHT IN IRISH VICTORY.

text.p: Striker Ian Dowie ended his recent goal drought by scoring both goals in Northern Ireland's 2-0 World Cup victory over Albania on Saturday.

The West Ham forward, who has failed to score in the premier league all season, took his international tally to 10 from 39 games with two early goals which effectively killed off the group nine match.

After 12 minutes he met a Steve Lomas cross with a firm downward header into the Albanian net, and then, nine minutes later, got the crucial final touch with his chest in a goalmouth scramble to put the Irish 2-0 up.
Dowie was denied a hat-trick in the second half when he crashed a header against a post.
"It was a magnificent team performance," he said afterwards. "I thought, as long as we could get an early goal it would settle us down, and that's what we did."
The win was Northern Ireland's first in the World Cup qualifiers and builds on their suprise 1-1 draw in Germany last month.
They move into third in the table, a point behind Ukraine, who have played one game less.
Germany, who were playing group leaders Portugal later on Saturday, are fourth, having played two games less than the Irish.

Northern Ireland - Tommy Wright, Ian Nolan, Gerry Taggart, Colin Hill, Barry Hunter, Kevin Horlock, Steve Morrow (Gerry McMahon 72), Steve Lomas, Iain Dowie (Jimmy Quinn 90), Neil Lennon, Michael Hughes.
